newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' Ramos leaves hospital. back to work.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' Ramos leaves hospital. back to work.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos, declaring he was in top shape, checked out of hospital and went back to work on Thursday, three days after an operation to remove a cholesterol lump blocking the flow of blood to his brain.

"Thank you, thank God. Back to work," the 68-year-old workaholic told reporters on his return to the presidential palace. He spoke briefly to his staff and and immediately began clearing a backlog of state papers, officials said.
Earlier, doctors, nurses and visitors cheered when Ramos, smiling and dressed in a dark jacket, came down to the lobby of the Makati Medical Centre and walked unaided to a black limousine.
"I am feeling very, very well," he said before being driven to his residence for a brief rest before proceeding to the palace.
"What's that?" he said, grinning, when asked if he would slow down.
Known to follow a punishing 18-hour work schedule daily, Ramos was advised by his chief doctor, Raul Fores, to ease up on his work load and also cut down on his intake of rich foods.
News that Ramos had checked out of the hospital buoyed the Manila bourse, helping push the main index 12.99 points up to 3,162.52 by the close.
The peso was also firmer in early trade, opening at 26.295 to the dollar from Tuesday's close of 26.297, and strengthened to 26.288 by mid-morning.
"Very soon," Ramos, an avid golfer, shouted back when a reporter asked when he would play golf again.
"He'll play golf in about 10 days' time," Fores told Reuters, adding however he had advised Ramos to cut down his pace and sleep longer.
"He is 68 years old. He cannot follow the schedule of a 20-year-old which was what he was doing. He wasn't sleeping enough," Fores said.
He said Ramos slept only about three hours a night, which he cut down to two hours in the weeks before hosting last month's summit of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum.
Fores blamed the high cholesterol level in the president's blood system on a diet of too much rich food.

"Lechon (roasted pig), everything, there's nothing he does not eat," the doctor added, when asked what Ramos had been eating before his cholesterol level shot up dangerously last weekend, prompting the emergency operation.

Ramos underwent surgery on Monday to remove a cholesterol blockage in his right carotid artery, one of the major passages for blood flowing to the brain. The affliction could have induced a massive stroke, doctors said.
But the operation was successful and the danger of recurrence of the illness was virtually nil, Fores said, adding blood checks on Thursday morning showed sharply lower cholesterol levels.
The day before the surgery, Ramos went to the hospital chapel to pray, Fores said, when asked if the president was nervous prior to the operation.
"I don't know if a gesture of prayer is an indication of being afraid," he said. "Anyone, regardless who he is, I suppose would pray before he gets operated on."
